metadata.title: ’Blue tsunami’ batters AI stocks: Is this a rare buy the dip setup?

content.text:
Investing.com -- Thursday's selloff was broad, and it started in AI. Pre-market bids suggest a partial bounce, but nothing has been confirmed yet.
The Day Everything Sold Off
-
S&P 500: closed at 7,353.73, down 4.36% (Nov 5, 3:59 PM EST). That is about 6.3% below its 52-week high of 7,844.52.
-
Nasdaq Composite: fell 5.52% to 24,315.00. It is down 11.9% over one month.
-
Philadelphia Semiconductor Index: fell 12.25% to 9,011.10. It is down 31.8% over one month, yet still up 28.4% over one year.
NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA): closed at $181.60 (-9.26%, Nov 5). Pre-market was $189.35 (+4.27%) as of Nov 6, 9:02 AM EST. Its 52-week range is $164.27–$243.37, and it is down 24.1% over one month.
What Triggered It
The trigger was Tuesday's Democratic sweep, the "blue tsunami". Investors feared tougher antitrust enforcement, environmental oversight and local pushback on power-hungry data centers. Read more (Nov 6, 2026)
-
Scale: An estimated $2.5T was wiped from the Nasdaq Composite, the biggest drop since March 2020. Read more (Nov 6, 2026)
-
Contagion: Japan's Nikkei closed 6% lower and entered a bear market. South Korea's KOSPI hit a circuit breaker. Read more (Nov 5, 2026)
-
Not just politics: Qualcomm fell nearly 10% on a smartphone chip sales miss. Anthropic's IPO is facing scrutiny and may be delayed.
The Dip-Buying Case
-
Strategists see overreaction. Yardeni Research called the selloff a "buying opportunity". It described the political backlash as "speed bumps, not roadblocks". Read more (Nov 6, 2026)
-
Spending is still strong. Reuters' Morning Bid noted that Marvell's $115B all-stock deal for Lumentum and Meta's $15B bond raise show no sign of an AI capex slowdown. Read more (Nov 6, 2026)
-
Futures point to relief. Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 0.9% earlier Friday.
The Bear Case
-
Forced selling may not be finished. One analysis warned that "there may be more pain to come" for chip and AI-equipment makers. It cited profit-taking and institutional deleveraging. Read more (Nov 6, 2026)
-
Regulation risk is slow-burning. A Democratic Congress could keep pressure on data-center buildouts for years.
-
Rates and data. Strong payrolls lifted Treasury yields, and the Bank of England just hiked. A hot jobs print would add a further headwind.
-
Valuation questions were already there. The AI trade had been under pressure for weeks before Thursday. Hedge funds were already cutting exposure, with selling shifting from the high-flyers to "anything with a ticker symbol".
